provenance: Four newly authored question texts, three learner profiles each. Prospective development diagnostic; no independent teacher or empirical gold labels.

cases.student_visible_text: 对每个正整数 n，证明 1+3+5+…+(2n−1)=n²。要求给出对任意 n 成立的证明，并解释为什么只验证 n=1、2、3 不能证明结论。可自行选择证明方法，不要求特定方法。
cases.learner_profile: 高中学生，能化简一元代数式，知道数学归纳法的基例与归纳步骤，已做过与此不同的简单归纳证明；未练习奇数求和、平方数图形或等差数列求和公式。

cases.student_visible_text:
An array a has at least one element and is sorted in nondecreasing order; duplicates are allowed. Integers and indexing are exact. Given target t, return the smallest index i with a[i] >= t, or len(a) if there is no such index. The following code is proposed:
l = 0
r = len(a) - 1
while l < r:
    m = (l + r) // 2
    if a[m] < t:
        l = m
    else:
        r = m
return l
Give one concrete input where it fails, repair it while retaining O(log n) worst-case running time, and justify both termination and the returned boundary for all allowed arrays, including duplicates and a target above all entries. You may change the interval convention. No library search function may be used.
cases.learner_profile: Undergraduates who can trace loops, understand sorted arrays, integer division, loop invariants and O(log n), and have traced ordinary binary search for an exact match. They have not implemented or proved a first-greater-or-equal boundary search or debugged its non-progress cases.

cases.student_visible_text: 以下均为虚构教学数据。200 名学生自愿选择是否参加辅导：参加组 100 人中 90 人通过考试，未参加组 100 人中 60 人通过。两组参加同一考试，记录无缺失。除此之外没有入学成绩、学习时间或其他背景数据。负责人说：“参加辅导让通过率增加了 30 个百分点。”计算观察到的通过率差；判断这些记录是否足以支持该因果结论，给出一个具体的替代解释，并提出一种能更可靠估计辅导因果效果的研究设计，说明它解决了什么问题。不得编造两组实际背景的差异。
cases.learner_profile: 大学入门统计学生，能计算比例和百分点差，理解“相关不等于因果”、混杂因素与随机分配的定义；还未将这些概念用于自愿参加项目的评价，也未自行设计随机对照研究。

cases.student_visible_text:
These sources describe a fictional station closure. A diary written on the announcement day says: "The manager said repairs should finish next week. I bought a weekly ticket because I trusted him." A maintenance log dated the same day says: "Parts have been ordered; the delivery date is not confirmed. Reopening depends on testing after installation." Twenty years later the diarist writes: "He knew the station would never reopen and deliberately deceived us." The station in fact never reopened. No record shows what information the manager received or what later prevented reopening.
Evaluate the later accusation using both contemporaneous sources. Give a plausible explanation consistent with deliberate deception and one consistent with an honest but mistaken forecast. Explain which parts are established and which remain hypotheses, how the time at which each source was written affects its evidential value, and what additional evidence would help distinguish the explanations. Conclude with a claim no stronger than the evidence permits. No outside historical knowledge is needed.
cases.learner_profile: First-year humanities students who can distinguish a reported observation from an inference and support a reading with a quotation. They have not practised weighing contemporaneous records against retrospective testimony or evaluating an accusation about another person’s prior knowledge.
